content.text: {"id": "mm7048a1", "data_focus": {"v": "yes", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "The economic costs were $2.2 trillion for fatal injuries and $2.0 trillion for nonfatal injuries"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "The number of injury deaths and associated economic cost were higher among males"}]}, "outcome_types": [{"v": "count/rate", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Injury count, rate per 100,000 population, cost by type (medical, work loss, value of statistical life, and quality of life loss)"}]}, {"v": "continuous", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "Costs are presented in 2019 U.S. dollars (USD)"}]}], "analytic_depth": [{"v": "summary", "ev": [{"loc": "summary", "q": "The estimated U.S. economic cost of injuries in 2019 was $4.2 trillion"}]}, {"v": "comparison", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "The 2019 economic cost of injuries ($4.2 trillion) is more than six times as high as a comparable estimate in 2013"}]}, {"v": "stratified/adjusted", "ev": [{"loc": "note", "q": "Age-adjusted rate is presented for “Total,” “Male,” and “Female” columns."}]}], "study_design": [{"v": "cost/economic", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "CDC estimated the economic cost of injuries that occurred in 2019 by assigning costs"}]}, {"v": "surveillance/descriptive", "ev": [{"loc": "text", "q": "WISQARS fatal injury counts are from CDC’s National Vital Statistics System mortality data"}]}], "methods_quotes": [{"loc": "text", "q": "were adjusted for patient clinical and demographic characteristics, including comorbidities, sex, and age"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "WISQARS nonfatal injury counts are hospital ED injury visits"}, {"loc": "text", "q": "Value of statistical life estimates were assigned by decedent age"}, {"loc": "note", "q": "Age-adjusted rate is presented for “Total,” “Male,” and “Female” columns."}], "confidence": "medium", "uncertain_fields": ["analytic_depth", "study_design"]}
